rows.abstract: The pot-bellied seahorse (Hippocampus abdominalis) is a high-value marine teleost, but its responses to dietary selenium (Se) remain poorly characterized. This 70-day trial evaluated nominal nano-selenium (Nano-Se) supplementation levels of 0, 10, 20, and 40 mg/kg; the unsupplemented frozen mysis shrimp contained 0.97 mg Se/kg on a wet-weight basis. Compared with the control, body weight gain and specific growth rate were higher, and feed conversion ratio was lower at 20 and 40 mg/kg. Additionally, body length gain was increased at 10 and 40 mg/kg. Tissue Se concentrations increased with supplementation and were highest in the liver. Nano-Se increased intestinal villus height and digestive enzyme activities; no overt histopathological lesions were observed in the examined sections. Intestinal 16S rRNA gene sequencing identified changes in microbial diversity and taxonomic composition. Untargeted lipidomics identified semi-quantitative changes in hepatic triglyceride-, phospholipid-, and ether-lipid-associated ion signals. Hepatic superoxide dismutase, catalase, and glutathione peroxidase activities were lower in supplemented groups than in the control. Catalase and superoxide dismutase activities were higher at 40 than at 20 mg/kg, whereas glutathione peroxidase did not differ between doses. Steady-state messenger RNA abundances of selenoprotein-related genes and whole-body sex steroid concentrations also changed. Overall, Nano-Se elicited dose- and endpoint-dependent responses, with no single dose consistently superior. The 10-20 mg/kg range warrants further evaluation, whereas 40 mg/kg maximized Se accumulation. These findings provide a basis for refining Nano-Se dose selection in seahorse aquaculture, although the optimal inclusion level and upper safe limit remain unresolved.

rows.abstract: Background and objective Severe acute malnutrition (SAM) remains a significant health challenge among children under five in India and is often complicated by parasitic infestations and deficiencies of neurotropic vitamins. These factors may contribute to developmental delay. This study assessed the association between parasitic infestations and neurotropic vitamin deficiencies with developmental delay in children with SAM in Datia district, Madhya Pradesh, India. Methods This hospital-based, cross-sectional observational study was conducted at the Nutritional Rehabilitation Centre (NRC) of the Government Medical College and its associated hospital in Datia district, Madhya Pradesh, India, from April 2022 to April 2024. Stool microscopy and blood investigations were performed to identify parasitic infections and estimate vitamin B1, B6, and holotranscobalamin (HoloTC) levels. Developmental status was assessed using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-IV). Data were analyzed using chi-square tests and logistic regression. Results Parasitic infections were detected in 30 (30%) children, with Ascaris lumbricoides identified in 10 (33%). Developmental delay was observed in 25 (71%) children with parasitic infections compared to 10 (29%) without infection. Mean vitamin levels were lower in infected than in non-infected children: vitamin B1 (0.132 ng/mL vs. 0.98 ng/mL), vitamin B6 (0.142 ng/mL vs. 0.768 ng/mL), and HoloTC (17 pmol/L vs. 27 pmol/L). On multivariate analysis, parasitic infection (adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 18.9, 95% CI: 5.2-68.2, p < 0.001) and HoloTC deficiency (aOR: 3.2, 95% CI: 1.05-9.7, p = 0.041) were independent predictors of developmental delay. Conclusions Parasitic infections and neurotropic vitamin deficiencies were strongly associated with developmental delay in children with SAM. Routine screening, deworming, and targeted nutritional interventions are essential to improve developmental outcomes in this vulnerable population.

rows.title: Patient-reported symptom profiles in vitamin B(12) deficiency and pernicious anemia: a cross-sectional study using latent class analysis.

rows.abstract: Pernicious anemia is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by impaired of vitamin B12 absorption and deficiency. Current diagnostic approaches rely on laboratory biomarkers with limitations in sensitivity and specificity, leading to diagnostic uncertainty and potentially delayed and/or suboptimal treatment. The 2024 NICE guidelines acknowledge that treatment frequency should be guided by individual symptom response rather than current one-size-fits-all schedules; however, the symptom heterogeneity underpinning this recommendation remains poorly characterized. We conducted secondary analysis of symptom survey data from 1,117 members of the Pernicious Anaemia Society (PAS) collected between August 2010 and November 2012. We applied latent class analysis (LCA) to 46 self-reported indicators comprising demographic characteristics, symptoms, and comorbid conditions, to identify distinct symptom-based subtypes and assess whether such subgroups can inform more tailored management of PA. Associations between symptom subtypes and diagnostic test results, age when symptoms first started, symptom duration, and treatment satisfaction were examined using chi-square and Fisher's exact tests. The best model included three distinct symptom subtypes: High Burden (n = 334, 29.9%), Moderate Burden (n = 613, 54.9%), and Low Burden (n = 170, 15.2%). The High Burden subtype exhibited fatigue (99.4%), cognitive dysfunction (97.9% memory loss), neurological manifestations (95.5% clumsiness), and suicidal thoughts (41.6%). Intrinsic factor antibody (IFA) status did not differ significantly across subtypes (χ 2 = 1.04, df = 2, p = 0.593). Age at symptom onset differed significantly across subtypes (p = 0.002), with the Low Burden subtype overrepresented in older age groups. The High Burden subtype had the longest diagnostic delays (56.9% >2 years). Standard three-monthly injections showed low satisfaction across all classes (High Burden: 8.5%, Moderate Burden: 23.7%, Low Burden: 30.7%). Symptom-based stratification identifies clinically meaningful subgroups independent of IFA status, supporting tailored, symptom-guided treatment rather than the current piecemeal approach. The inverse association between high symptom burden and age of onset warrants clinical attention. The co-occurrence of markedly elevated rates of depression and suicidal thoughts in the High Burden subtype suggest that integrated mental health assessments should form part of routine clinical management.

rows.title: Running on Empty: Relative Energy Deficiency in a Military Endurance Athlete.

rows.abstract: Relative Energy Deficiency in Sports (RED-S) is a clinical syndrome characterized by low caloric intake relative to energy expenditure, resulting in a cascade of endocrine, metabolic, and musculoskeletal consequences. In females, hallmark features include decreased bone mineral density and menstrual dysfunction, though the syndrome affects multiple organ systems in both sexes. We present the case of a 22-year-old active-duty military member who suffered recurrent stress fractures, irregular menstrual cycles, and chronic fatigue that impacted her duty status. She was noted to have a long history of non-intentional calorie restriction and was eventually diagnosed with RED-S. Treatment consisted of a multidisciplinary approach, resulting in objective improvement in bone density and a successful return to full duty status. This case highlights the importance of early diagnosis and appropriate treatment of RED-S among military members to decrease morbidity and prevent limitations to military readiness and career progression.

rows.title: Effects of early gestational parenteral iron administration on maternal iron biomarkers and reproductive performance in sows under commercial conditions.
rows.discovery_query: ((vitamin[Title/Abstract] OR mineral[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract] OR selenium[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin B12"[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin D"[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR status[Title/Abstract] OR intake[Title/Abstract])) AND 2022:2026[pdat] AND hasabstract[text] NOT retracted publication[pt] NOT case reports[pt]
rows.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of early-gestation parenteral iron dextran administration on maternal iron status and reproductive performance in sows under commercial conditions. A total of 235 TN70 sows (parities 1 to 9, average parity 4.2) were enrolled in early gestation (30 ± 2 days of gestation) and followed through pre-weaning (19 ± 2 days of lactation). Sows were allotted by parity and initial blood hemoglobin (Hb) to one of three parenteral iron dextran treatments initiated at enrollment: 0 mg (CONFe; n = 77), administered without injection; 2500 mg (MODFe; n = 79), administered as a single 12.5-mL intramuscular injection; or 5000 mg (HIGHFe; n = 79), administered as two 12.5-mL intramuscular injections (2500 mg per injection), with injections administered into the trapezius muscle. Blood Hb was measured on days 30 (enrollment) and 112 ± 2 days of gestation (pre-farrow) and day 19 ± 2 days of lactation (pre-weaning) using a HemoCue Hb 201 + system via ear-vein sampling. A subset of sows (N = 75; 25 per treatment) had jugular blood samples collected for analysis of serum iron, ferritin, total iron-binding capacity (TIBC), and plasma C-reactive protein (CRP). On day 112 of gestation, blood Hb and serum ferritin increased as iron dosage increased (linear, P = 0.016 and P = 0.046, respectively), whereas serum TIBC decreased (linear, P = 0.021). On day 19 of lactation, serum ferritin increased as iron dosage increased (linear, P = 0.036). Total born and liveborn piglets were not affected by treatment. However, stillborn rate tended to decrease as iron dosage increased (linear, P = 0.068). When evaluated within parity, stillborn rate decreased as iron dosage increased in parity 1 sows (linear, P = 0.024) and tended to decrease in sows of parity 5 or greater (linear, P = 0.097), whereas no responses were observed in intermediate parities. In conclusion, parenteral administration of iron dextran during early gestation improved sow iron status through weaning, with the greatest response generally observed at 5000 mg. Stillborn rate also tended to decrease as iron dosage increased, with responses most evident in parity 1 sows and sows of parity 5 or greater.

rows.title: Anti-CaSR egg yolk antibody improves calcium absorption and bone mineral deposition through intestinal CaSR modulation.
rows.discovery_query: ((vitamin[Title/Abstract] OR mineral[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract] OR selenium[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin B12"[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin D"[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR status[Title/Abstract] OR intake[Title/Abstract])) AND 2022:2026[pdat] AND hasabstract[text] NOT retracted publication[pt] NOT case reports[pt]
rows.abstract: Calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) is a key negative regulator of intestinal calcium transport, and targeting CaSR represents a promising strategy to improve mineral retention. Egg yolk antibodies can be used as a feed-based approach to modulate intestinal physiological processes. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate whether anti-CaSR egg yolk antibodies could modulate intestinal calcium transport and enhance calcium and phosphorus retention in broilers. Hy-Line Brown laying hens were immunized over a 4-week period with either a CaSR peptide vaccine or an adjuvant control (without CaSR peptide). High titers of anti-CaSR antibodies were detected in egg yolk at week 5, indicating successful antibody production. The egg yolks were subsequently collected, freeze-dried into powder, and incorporated into broiler diets at a supplementation level of 0.5%. A 14-day feeding trial demonstrated that dietary supplementation with anti-CaSR antibodies markedly increased serum calcium and phosphorus levels, improved apparent ileal digestibility of both minerals, and enhanced tibial ash as well as calcium and phosphorus deposition. Mechanistically, dietary supplementation with anti-CaSR antibodies upregulated components of the transcellular calcium transport pathway, including transient receptor potential vanilloid 5 (TRPV5) and calbindin-D28k (CaBP-D28k), and elevated serum calcitriol level, indicating activation of a vitamin D-dependent regulatory axis. Furthermore, anti-CaSR increased the expression of key phosphate transporters in both the intestine and kidney, supporting its broader role in mineral homeostasis. These findings demonstrate that anti-CaSR antibodies enhance the expression of calcium and phosphorus transport proteins, thereby improving mineral retention and promoting bone mineralization in broilers.

rows.abstract: Efficient peripheral blood stem cell (PBSC) collection from healthy donors is essential for transplantation success and donor safety. While hemoglobin is routinely used in donor evaluation, the contribution of iron-related biomarkers and red cell indices to predicting collection outcomes remains incompletely defined. In this retrospective cohort study, 143 healthy PBSC donors undergoing granulocyte colony-stimulating factor-mediated mobilization and apheresis were evaluated. Baseline hematologic parameters and iron-related biomarkers were analyzed in relation to weight-adjusted total CD34+ cell yield using correlation, threshold-based analyses, and multivariable modeling. The median donor age was 32 years, and 70.6% were male. The overall median CD34+ yield was 5.41 × 106/kg. Ferritin negatively correlated with CD34+ yield in male donors (r = -0.22, p = 0.027). In female donors, folate levels and red cell distribution width showed positive correlations with collection outcomes (r = 0.342, p = 0.027; r = 0.322, p = 0.037). The Mentzer index demonstrated an inverse association with CD34+ yield across both sexes. Transferrin saturation ≥ 18% in females was associated with higher target achievement rates (95.2% vs. 66.7%, p = 0.020). In males, ferritin ≥ 73 μg/L or hemoglobin > 15.3 g/dL was associated with lower collection success. Readily available red cell indices and iron parameters are associated with clinically relevant PBSC collection outcomes and may serve as practical biomarkers for predicting PBSC collection performance and improving donor assessment. Incorporation of these markers into donor assessment may improve collection planning and procedural efficiency.

rows.title: Iron-dependent metabolic rewiring drives tryptophan-associated melanin production in a clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain.
rows.discovery_query: ((vitamin[Title/Abstract] OR mineral[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract] OR selenium[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin B12"[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin D"[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR status[Title/Abstract] OR intake[Title/Abstract])) AND 2022:2026[pdat] AND hasabstract[text] NOT retracted publication[pt] NOT case reports[pt]
rows.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a human opportunistic pathogen, capable of producing a wide range of metabolites, including pyomelanin, which results from alterations in tyrosine catabolism. In contrast, melanin synthesis from tryptophan has never been reported in Pseudomonas. In this study, we applied an integrated multi-omics approach to characterize physiological adaptations associated with the emergence of a tryptophan-associated melanin-like pigment in P. aeruginosa PAH, a persistently re-isolated strain from a cystic fibrosis patient. Structural analysis revealed the production of a previously unreported melanin-like polymer produced under tryptophan supplementation, coexisting with a pyomelanin-like soluble fraction. This melanin exhibited iron-reduction capacity, supporting a potential physiological role in iron acquisition within the infective niche. Genome analysis identified mutations affecting iron acquisition, including genes involved in pyoverdine biosynthesis. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a coordinated reprogramming of iron homeostasis, characterized not only by the downregulation of pyoverdine-associated genes but also by altered expression of alternative siderophore systems and a broader set of genes, such as redox response pathways. Non-targeting metabolomic analyses uncovered the accumulation of indole-derived compounds. Inhibitors of tyrosine and tryptophan catabolism demonstrated a metabolic shift between these pathways. Notably, iron availability emerged as a key regulator of this system, with iron limitation promoting pigment production and associated metabolic states. Integrating these data sets, we developed an integrative model linking iron homeostasis, genomic variation, transcriptional and metabolic reprogramming, and melanin production in P. aeruginosa PAH. Overall, tryptophan arises as a key compound for melanin production in a Pseudomonas strain, expanding the diversity of melanins synthesized by this genus.IMPORTANCEThis study reveals a previously unrecognized way by which Pseudomonas aeruginosa can produce melanin, a protective pigment linked to survival and persistence in hostile environments. Here, we report how a novel melanin pigment, produced in tryptophan-supplemented media, can reduce iron and is linked to iron homeostasis in a clinical P. aeruginosa strain. Employing a multi-omics approach, we show that this pathway operates primarily through anthranilate and indolic intermediates and is favored under iron-limited conditions. This finding deepens current understanding about pigment diversity in bacteria and highlights the remarkable metabolic flexibility of P. aeruginosa during infection. Since the same phenotype was observed again in year-later isolates from the same patient, our results suggest a potential role of this trait in long-term infection and adaptation.

rows.abstract: Adequate vitamin B12 (B12) concentrations are essential for optimal pregnancy development. The COVID-19 pandemic may have compromised adequate B12 intake. However, evidence on maternal B12 status and its predictors during the pandemic is scarce. This study aimed to assess serum total B12 (sB12) concentrations in the first or second trimester, and to identify maternal lifestyle, obstetric, and dietary predictors of B12 status among pregnant Chilean women during the COVID-19 pandemic. Between March 2020 and November 2021, pregnant women (≥18 years) were recruited from public healthcare centers in Santiago, Chile, to participate in the Chilean Maternal and Infant Cohort Study-II (CHIMINCs-II). The sB12 concentration was determined in a randomly selected sample of 413 participants who provided blood samples in the first or second trimester, using a chemiluminescent microparticle immunoassay. B12 deficiency was defined as sB12 concentrations <148 pmol/L. Stepwise linear and logistic regression models were used to identify predictors of B12 status. The median (IQR) sB12 concentration was 169 (106) pmol/L, and 37% of women had B12 deficiency. Overall, 40% of women had obesity. Women who took prenatal supplements and had a higher income were less likely to have a B12 deficiency (p <0.05). Higher pre-pregnancy BMI and parity were associated with a higher likelihood of B12 deficiency. Maternal B12 deficiency was concentrated among vulnerable groups. Efforts should be made to identify and support these groups before and during pregnancy to improve maternal B12 status, especially under food insecurity scenarios, such as during the COVID-19 pandemic.

rows.title: Integrative physiological and transcriptomic analyses reveal key metabolic pathway responses in wax gourd (Benincasa hispida) leaves under potassium deficiency and excess.

rows.abstract: Potassium (K) is a key nutrient for increasing yield, improving quality, and enhancing stress resistance in wax gourd (Benincasa hispida). However, the phenotypic, physiological, ecological, and molecular adaptation mechanisms of wax gourd under different K levels remain poorly understood. In this study, a field experiment was conducted with three treatments, i.e., K deficiency (K0), moderate K (300 kg K2O hm-2, K300), and excessive K (500 kg K2O hm-2, K500), to evaluate the effects of K fertilization on the morphology, physiology, and transcriptomics of wax gourd. Results showed that compared with K300, K0 and K500 reduced wax gourd yield by 25.22% and 10.38%, respectively. Fruit soluble sugar, soluble protein, titratable acidity, vitamin C, and dry matter content were all significantly decreased under K0 treatment. Both K0 and K500 damaged chloroplast ultrastructure, induced stomatal closure, and reduced photosynthetic efficiency. Under K0, the activities of Rubisco, sucrose phosphate synthase (SPS), and ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase (AGPase) decreased by 50.79%-60.30%, 58.75%-61.11%, and 51.20%-54.00%, respectively, while photosynthetic K-use efficiency (PKUE) and K accumulation decreased by 1.54%-22.70% and 25.67%-65.95%. Collectively, K deficiency exacerbated yield and quality reduction by inhibiting photosynthesis and K+ uptake/utilization. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that under K deficiency, genes associated with photosynthesis, photosynthetic antenna proteins, nitrogen metabolism, and starch and sucrose metabolism were downregulated, whereas genes associated with antioxidant enzyme activity and plant hormone signal transduction (ABA and CTK) were upregulated. Under excess K, genes encoding various transporters, as well as those involved in starch and sucrose metabolism, were downregulated. In conclusion, among the tested K levels, K300 (300 kg K2O hm-2) showed the best overall performance in wax gourd cultivation, contributing to synergistic improvements in yield, quality, and fertilizer efficiency. This study offers both theoretical insights and practical guidance for elucidating K-stress response mechanisms and for optimizing K-fertilizer strategies in wax gourd.

rows.abstract: Vitamin B1 status is typically assessed by measuring whole blood thiamine diphosphate (TDP). However, volumetric expression (nmol/L) may be misleading in anemia or polycythemia, as TDP is primarily carried within erythrocytes. While hemoglobin-normalized TDP (ng/g Hb) may provide a more robust biomarker-less influenced by hematological variations-reference interval (RI) data are scarce. Thus, we aimed to establish RIs for Hb-normalized TDP and evaluate the impact of its expression (ng/g Hb vs. nmol/L) on thiamine status classification. RIs for Hb-normalized TDP were established using 130 healthy adults (18-65 years) per CLSI EP28-A3c. Exclusion criteria included vitamin B1 supplementation, denutrition, hepatic disease, and other conditions affecting thiamine metabolism. TDP was quantified via HPLC with fluorescence detection. Outliers were excluded using Tukey's and Dixon's methods. A retrospective analysis of 5429 routine samples assessed reclassification rates using Cohen's weighted kappa and the net reclassification index (NRI). The Hb-normalized TDP RI was 249-531 ng/g Hb (90% CI: 241-268, 519-557), and the volumetric RI was 88-181 nmol/L (90% CI: 83-92, 175-189). The units were strongly correlated (r = 0.829, p 〈10-33). No sex- or age-specific partitioning was required (z = 2.14, z* = 3.12). Among routine samples, the reclassification rate was 11.3% (weighted κ = 0.682, good agreement), with an NRI of 8.58%. Notably, 88% of reclassifications were upward, and 68.5% of samples with low TDP in nmol/L were normal in ng/g Hb. The reclassification rate rose to 25.8% in anemic patients. We established RI for Hb-normalized TDP according to CLSI methodology. Our findings support adopting ng/g Hb for TDP assessment, particularly in anemic patients.

rows.title: Gut microbiota-expressed sulfotransferase sulfonates 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 and promotes depression.
rows.discovery_query: ((vitamin[Title/Abstract] OR mineral[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract] OR selenium[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin B12"[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin D"[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR status[Title/Abstract] OR intake[Title/Abstract])) AND 2022:2026[pdat] AND hasabstract[text] NOT retracted publication[pt] NOT case reports[pt]
rows.abstract: Vitamin D deficiency (VDD) has been associated with depressive symptoms, but the underlying cause of this deficiency remains unclear. Here, we isolated and cultured Escherichia coli (E. coli) from the feces of depressive patients with VDD and found that this bacterium could metabolize 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 (25[OH]D3) in vitro. In vivo, oral gavage of E. coli induced a decline in circulating 25[OH]D3 levels and elicited depressive-like behaviors in mice. The gene encoding the 25[OH]D3-metabolizing enzyme in E. coli was identified as a sulfotransferase (SULT). A recombinant strain engineered for heterologous expression of SULT similarly reduced serum 25[OH]D3 levels and induced depressive-like behaviors. Interestingly, 25[OH]D3-3-sulfate, the sulfonation product of 25[OH]D3, also produced depressive-like behaviors in mice. Finally, both the prevalence of E. coli and the abundance of the SULT gene were strongly increased in depressive patients when compared to healthy controls. Our findings indicate that SULT expressed by gut microbiota may contribute to depressive symptoms by promoting 25[OH]D3 sulfonation and increasing 25[OH]D3-3-sulfate levels. However, further clinical and mechanistic studies are required to translate these findings to human depression.

rows.abstract: Dengue fever, a significant health concern in tropical regions, including India, presents in healthcare settings with a disease spectrum ranging from mild to severe illness. Anti-body dependent enhancement (ADE) and non-ADE mechanism such as nutrition (vitamin D, etc.) have been suggested for dengue severity. The relationship between vitamin D, a known immune modulator, and the severity of dengue fever in pediatric patients was investigated. This prospective study, enrolled 99 children aged 1-18 years with confirmed dengue fever between April 2023 and September 2024. Patients were classified into dengue fever (DF) or those with complications, including, "Dengue with Warning Signs (DWS) and Severe Dengue (SD)." Serum vitamin D levels were measured at admission, and clinical outcomes and laboratory parameters were analyzed. The ROC curve analysis was used to evaluate vitamin D's ability to predict complications. Patients having DF with complications, i.e., DWS and SD, had lower vitamin D levels (Median 13.5 ng/ml vs. 21.5 ng/ml) than DF patients. Those with vitamin D levels <20 ng/ml had a 3.3-fold higher risk of complications (p = 0.01). A vitamin D cutoff of 17.9 ng/ml predicted severity with moderate accuracy (AUC = 0.683). Severe cases required longer hospital stays and more intensive care but had full recovery. Vitamin D deficiency is linked to greater dengue severity in children. Addressing this modifiable risk factor could help reduce severe outcomes, emphasizing the potential role of supplementation in dengue management.

rows.title: Maternal calcium deficiency and offspring programming: mechanistic and translational insights.
rows.discovery_query: ((vitamin[Title/Abstract] OR mineral[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract] OR selenium[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin B12"[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin D"[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR status[Title/Abstract] OR intake[Title/Abstract])) AND 2022:2026[pdat] AND hasabstract[text] NOT retracted publication[pt] NOT case reports[pt]
rows.abstract: Maternal calcium deficiency during pregnancy and lactation may predispose offspring to metabolic, skeletal, and cardiovascular disorders in the context of the Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) paradigm. Experimental evidence from rodent models under severe or extreme calcium restriction, particularly studies by Takaya and colleagues, indicates that such conditions can induce insulin resistance, impair bone metabolism, and produce sex-specific cardiometabolic phenotypes in offspring. These effects appear to involve impaired placental calcium transport, altered expression of plasma membrane Ca-ATPase (PMCA) isoforms, and changes in parathyroid hormone, vitamin D, and calcium-sensing receptor signaling, together with persistent epigenetic modifications in hepatic 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 (Hsd11b1) and related genes. In humans, however, active placental calcium transport and maternal homeostatic adaptations generally keep fetal calcium concentrations higher than maternal concentrations, and direct evidence that modest maternal calcium deficiency alone causes fetal hypocalcemia remains limited. Nonetheless, observational studies and supplementation trials in populations with low calcium intake, including Gambian cohorts and WHO-endorsed preeclampsia-prevention studies, support the importance of adequate maternal calcium, often together with vitamin D, for maternal health and possibly for offspring growth and blood pressure regulation. This mini-review synthesizes mechanistic, epidemiological, and micronutrient-DOHaD evidence to inform preventive and research strategies.

rows.title: Photosystem I structural fusion with IsiA enhances light-harvesting capabilities of filamentous cyanobacterium during iron deficiency.
rows.discovery_query: ((vitamin[Title/Abstract] OR mineral[Title/Abstract] OR magnesium[Title/Abstract] OR zinc[Title/Abstract] OR iron[Title/Abstract] OR selenium[Title/Abstract] OR folate[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin B12"[Title/Abstract] OR "vitamin D"[Title/Abstract]) AND (deficiency[Title/Abstract] OR supplementation[Title/Abstract] OR status[Title/Abstract] OR intake[Title/Abstract])) AND 2022:2026[pdat] AND hasabstract[text] NOT retracted publication[pt] NOT case reports[pt]
rows.abstract: During iron stress, cyanobacteria produce iron-stress-inducible protein A (IsiA), which associates with photosystem I (PSI) to support cell growth. In most cyanobacteria, the stress induces formation of large IsiA18-PSI3 complexes. However, some species, including Anabaena sp. PCC 7120, studied in this work, form an unusual, smaller PSI-monomer-based IsiA-PSI supercomplex containing a unique fusion of IsiA with the PSI subunit PsaL, IsiA-PsaL. In this study, genetically tagged IsiA-PsaL was used to isolate several IsiA-PsaL-containing supercomplexes composed of multiple IsiA homologs. A combination of static and time-resolved optical spectroscopies was used to evaluate the energetic properties of gel-embedded supercomplexes, including the excitation energy transfer efficiency from IsiA-PsaL to PSI. These analyses demonstrated that excitation energy transfer in the IsiA-PsaL complex is highly efficient. Enhanced efficiency may be a key factor underlying the downsizing of the IsiA-PSI assembly, which could compensate for the smaller size of the complex.
